name: Thoko and the Can That Wouldn’t Grow
shortDescription: Thoko learns why litter does not belong in farmland when one discarded can sparks an unforgettable lesson about crops, waste, recycling and caring for the land.
longDescription: After helping in the fields, Thoko rides home with her father on an ox wagon carrying maize. When she throws an empty drink can into a field, her father gently asks what she thinks will grow from it. Thoko imagines the can taking root and becoming an enormous tree made from rubbish, helping her understand the difference between living crops and manufactured waste. She retrieves the can, joins other children in a supervised clean-up, and learns how waste can be sorted for reuse, recycling, composting and safe disposal. The cleaned field is planted again, showing how small responsible choices can protect food-producing land, animals, soil and water.

attribution.author: Khothatso Ranoosi and Marion Drew
attribution.adaptationNote: Adapted for animation by Panda Kids Club. Changes were made, including modernised waste-management guidance, a generic beverage can, supervised safe clean-up practices, and a revised ending focused on sorting, reuse, recycling, composting and approved waste collection.
